title: Ordinary realization of the exceptional constant derived pair
statement: For the same separated finite-type model, compactification and exceptional system as [def-sf-coefficient-endpoint-objects], there exists realization data [def-sf-coefficient-realization-cohomology-data] such that, for every native exceptional right adjunction, the underlying ordinary derived pair of J applied to the native point constant is isomorphic to the realized exceptional constant pair. This is a derived-pair assertion before taking any cohomology degree and asserts no Tate endpoint.

proof.text: For every supplied J and adjunction, form gamma, the fixed ordinary right mate of A.left. The reference-transport theorem proves that gamma is invertible using the existing reference package and coefficient-change equivalences.

proof.text: Transpose both action-intertwining composites through the coefficient adjunction. Counit naturality and mateEquiv_counit replace the exceptional mate by beta inverse followed by the Frobenius of the counit. Naturality of beta moves gamma past that inverse. Its counit equation replaces F(gamma) followed by the counit by A.left inverse followed by the forgotten native counit. The latter is equivariant by the morphism law of A.targetModel. A.left_frobenius makes the two transposes equal; adjunction injectivity proves the right-action equation. This is the complete private right_mate_intertwines calculation in Lean. The exceptionalIso definition is exactly the inverse-exchange mate.

proof.text: Lift the invertible ordinary mate to coefficient Frobenius pairs using its action equation and reflection of isomorphisms by forgetting. At the native point constant, compose with the image of A.pointUnit. Apply CoefficientRealization.pairs to this composite and precompose the inverse of A.sourceRealization. The private exceptionalConstant_eq_map equation identifies the endpoint with the literal exceptionalConstant definition, proving the required isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem exceptional_realization :
    ∃ R : CoefficientRealization.Data P X₀,
      ∀ (J : WeilComplex P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l (Spec (.of P.field.k₀)) ⥤
          WeilComplex P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l X₀.left)
        (adj : WeilComplex.derivedLowerShriek P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l X₀.hom ⊣ J),
        Nonempty
          ((NativePairCohomology.native P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l X₀.left).obj
              (J.obj (WeilSheaf.toComplex.obj
                (WeilSheaf.adicConstant P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l
                  (Spec (.of P.field.k₀))))) ≅
            (CoefficientRealization.pairs P X₀ R).obj (exceptionalConstant P X₀ c₀ S))
